To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a novel set SNPs at the well-known breast cancer risk locus 6q25 in an expanded study of Latinas.
we identified novel common variants at 6q24 that were associated with breast cancer risk in Latinas and that we replicated this association in Latinas and in other ancestries.
we have identified a novel set (SNP, rs3778608, rs3778607 and rs3778609) of SNPs at 6q24 associated with breast cancer risk in Latinas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying genetic variants for breast and ovarian cancer risk.
the genetic basis of cancer in Latinas.
the identification and characterization of genetic variants that are associated with the risk of breast cancer in Latinas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our study adds to evidence that the 6q locus is important for breast cancer susceptibility and highlights the utility of additional searches for genetic risk variants in non-European populations.

our study adds to evidence that the 6q24.1-24.2 locus is important for breast cancer susceptibility and that our study highlights the utility of additional searches for genetic breast cancer susceptibility variants in non-European populations.
our study adds to evidence that the 6q22.33 locus is associated with breast cancer, but the specific causal variant is still not identified.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we identified a novel common breast cancer susceptibility variant in the 6q24.2 locus, rs3778608, which has been previously shown to be associated with breast cancer in Latinas and is also associated in Latinas of European and African ancestry.

we identified a novel set (n = 6) of SNPs associated with breast cancer risk at 6q24.2 in Latinas and replicated the effect in women of Latin-American ancestry and in women of African, East Asian and European ancestry.
we identified 3 new common breast cancer variants in the 6q22.33 region, rs3778606, rs3778607 and rs3778609.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic architecture of breast cancer is more complex than we thought.
the genetic architecture of breast cancer susceptibility is likely to be more complex than previously thought.
the 6q22.1 locus, which is strongly associated with breast cancer risk, is enriched for variants of indigenous American origin.
